key_insight: PhysForge decouples functional logic and physical realism to generate 3D assets that are not just geometrically plausible but behaviorally usable in interactive worlds, enabled by a large physics-annotated dataset.
problem_solved: Existing 3D asset generation focuses on static geometry and ignores functional/physical properties required for interaction, making assets unsuitable for embodied agents and interactive simulations.
method: Two-stage, decoupled pipeline: (1) synthesize functional/hierarchical object specifications (functional logic) and (2) generate physics-grounded 3D geometry, materials, and physical parameters.
Train and validate using PhysDB — a large-scale dataset (~150,000 assets) annotated with a four-tier physics hierarchy to supervise functional and physical attributes.
Use physics-aware rendering/simulation checks to ensure generated assets afford intended interactions and exhibit stable dynamic behavior.
impact: Provides a practical route to produce interactive-ready 3D assets for virtual worlds and embodied AI, reducing manual authoring and enabling more realistic training and evaluation of agents.

paper_title: PhysForge: Generating Physics-Grounded 3D Assets for Interactive Virtual World
paper_authors: Yunhan Yang, Chunshi Wang, Junliang Ye, Yang Li, Zanxin Chen
